preflight.note: Registered before implementation or build for the engine identity defect. The initial finding review used existing source and evidence only; no implementation build or full test run was started.

acceptance_criteria.text: Compare and record a deterministic semantic-contract identity design before implementation. Distinguish transport protocol compatibility, product release identity, semantic validation compatibility, and executable authenticity; define the identity's authoritative inputs, versioning, migration behavior, and limits.

Implement the approved semantic identity in the Rust engine handshake and Python client. Same-protocol, same-product-version engines with a missing or mismatched semantic identity fail closed for canonical operations in ordinary package discovery and when selected through REPOPACT_ENGINE; developer override behavior is explicit and cannot silently bypass the check.

Add focused tests proving a stale same-version engine is rejected and a matching engine is accepted, covering ordinary Scripts-directory discovery, explicit development override, missing identity, mismatch, and the agreed compatibility/migration boundary.
Verify package/build wiring provides the same deterministic semantic identity to Python and Rust for source and wheel builds, without treating the identity as proof of trusted executable bytes.

Document the four identity guarantees, mismatch behavior, override rules, and migration path. Explicitly state that a semantic ID detects accidental version skew but does not authenticate a maliciously substituted binary; any trusted-artifact verification remains a separate design and approval.

Record exact source commit, product/protocol/semantic identities, executable digest, and focused validation results so the built engine used for conformance can be independently correlated with its source. Preserve prior historical evidence unchanged.
Link this work to WI074/RPS-016 as supporting Core/Workbench compatibility evidence. Do not change RPS-016 to satisfied; its full acceptance remains independently pending after this work completes.

Before any build, record a fresh disk-space budget, expected peak temporary output, selected target/temp paths, and whether generated outputs will be retained or cleaned. Prefer focused tests and reuse; do not run concurrent or duplicate Cargo builds for unchanged sources.
